label: fact-check
system: You fact-check the surprise claims planned for a short explainer video, before its narration is written. For each claim: verdict "keep" if the research notes support it as written; "reword" if the true version is close (give the claim with exactly the wording and numbers the sources support, e.g. "over 600 gallons" for a rounded figure, "New England" instead of a wrong state); "drop" if it is false, unsupported or a myth. Judge ONLY from the research notes (a claim they do not support is dropped) and copy the source URLs from them (url and title) for keep and reword. Write each claim the way the narrator will say it: no abbreviations (never "US", "U.S." or "USA": "American", "in America"; an agency without the country: "the Department of Energy", "the Army Corps of Engineers").

**Claim 0: a 90 mph wind exerts about 20 pounds per square foot. Supported in a corrected form.**
- Penn State AE thesis appendix (wind pressure table, q = 0.00256 V^2): 20.7 psf at 90 mph. URL: https://www.engr.psu.edu/ae/Thesis/portfolios/2006/hsm117/Final%20Report/Appendix%20A.pdf
- Eng-Tips: 0.00256 comes from standard air density. URL: https://www.eng-tips.com/viewthread.cfm?qid=4103
- This is the basic velocity pressure; design codes then apply factors. Corrected: "A 90 mile per hour wind pushes about 20 pounds on every square foot."

**Claim 1: post footings must reach below the frost line so frost heave does not lift them. Supported in a corrected form.**
- IRC R403.1.4 summary: footings must extend below the frost line, and at least 12 inches below grade. URL: https://www.jaspector.com/codes/irc-2021/ch04-foundations/footing-depth-frost-line-requirements/
- Decks.com footing depth guide: footings below the frost line to prevent frost heave. URL: https://www.decks.com/how-to/articles/deck-footing-frost-depth-map
- Otsego MN: footing base at least 42 inches below finished grade. URL: https://www.otsegomn.gov/DocumentCenter/View/106/Deck-PDF
- Some freestanding structures are exempt; local codes rule. Corrected: "Footings usually go below the frost line, so frost cannot heave them up."

**Claim 2: paving slabs are laid on a compacted sub-base. Supported as written.**
- Wickes, lay a patio: at least 100 mm of compacted MOT Type 1 sub-base. URL: https://www.wickes.co.uk/how-to-guides/garden-landscaping/lay-a-patio
- Bradstone: 150 mm compacted sub-base then a mortar bed. URL: https://www.bradstone.com/homeowner/blog/how-to-lay-paving-slabs-for-your-patio
